/accessibility.title: Accessibility — Esgrow Studio
/accessibility.description: Accessibility. Thoughtful digital services from Esgrow Studio.
/accessibility.main:
THE LITTLE THINGS

Accessibility

Clear information about this website and how it works.

Let’s grow together ↗

Our approach

We aim for clear navigation, readable content and usable experiences across screen sizes. Accessibility is part of ongoing design and development rather than a one-time task.

Features on this website

Navigation and forms use semantic HTML, interactive controls have visible focus styles, and animations respect the reduced-motion setting. Touch and keyboard scrolling retain native behaviour.

Motion preferences

Enable reduced motion in your device or browser preferences to disable entrance effects and wheel momentum. You can navigate using a keyboard without using a mouse.

Known limitations

The site has not undergone an independent accessibility audit. Some decorative text and generated imagery may need further review. This statement is not a claim of certified compliance.

Feedback

A verified business contact channel for accessibility feedback must be added before public commercial launch.

THE LITTLE THINGS

Privacy policy

Clear information about this website and how it works.

Let’s grow together ↗

About this notice

This notice describes the current website. It is a draft pending confirmation of Esgrow Studio’s legal business identity, address and privacy contact before accepting online inquiries.

What the forms do

If you submit an inquiry and the server confirms receipt, your name, email, optional business details, chosen service, message and consent are stored in the studio’s configured MongoDB database so the studio can review and respond. Downloading a brief instead creates a local file without submitting it. Avoid entering sensitive personal information.

Hosting and external resources

The hosting provider may process technical request information to serve and protect the site. The website loads fonts from Google Fonts, which involves a request to Google. Provider terms and privacy notices also apply to those services.

Cookies and tracking

No analytics or advertising trackers have been added to this website. See the cookie policy for the current browser-storage behaviour.

Your information

You can clear unsent entries by refreshing or closing the page, and delete downloaded briefs from your device. For submitted inquiries, the studio must provide a verified contact for access, correction and deletion requests before accepting commercial inquiries. A retention period has not yet been finalised and must be set before launch.

Changes

This notice should be reviewed whenever forms, analytics, integrations or hosting arrangements change.

Web & strategy · Esgrow Studio

Before you redesign, ask better questions.

Practical thoughts from the studio.

Let’s grow together ↗

Start with the job your website needs to do.

A redesign is more useful when it begins with a business problem. Are visitors struggling to understand your offer, find a service or take the next step? List the friction before choosing the visual direction.

Make an inventory before you make a moodboard.

Review your pages, content, forms and integrations. Decide what must stay, what can be simplified and who owns each piece of content. This makes the scope clearer for everyone.

Choose a few signals to review.

Agree what you will observe after launch: completed inquiries, useful engagement or a clearer path to key information. A new look is one part of the experience; clear content and dependable implementation matter too.

Keep exploring.

/blog/connected-marketing.main:
Marketing · Esgrow Studio

Why your website and ads need the same conversation.

Practical thoughts from the studio.

Let’s grow together ↗

Follow the promise through.

An ad sets an expectation. The landing page should continue that thought with the same offer, language and visual cues. A disconnected experience asks the visitor to start over.

Give every page a useful next step.

Match the action to the intent. Someone exploring an unfamiliar service may need details and answers before they are ready to inquire. Keep the next step clear without hiding the information they need.

Review the whole journey.

A campaign review should consider the creative, audience, landing experience and inquiry process together. Treat results as signals to investigate rather than reasons to change everything at once.

Keep exploring.

/blog/website-care.main:
Studio notes · Esgrow Studio

A practical rhythm for looking after your website.

Practical thoughts from the studio.

Let’s grow together ↗

Keep a small, consistent routine.

Check your key pages, navigation and forms regularly. Review outdated information, broken links and any changes to third-party tools that your site depends on.

Plan updates and recovery together.

Before changing a platform or integration, understand how you would recover if something went wrong. Keep a suitable backup process and document who can access it.

Make ownership clear.

Assign responsibility for domains, hosting, content and support requests. A short record of providers, renewal dates and approved contacts can remove a surprising amount of uncertainty.

Keep exploring.
